declared.title: Not Learning From Failure—the Greatest Failure of All
declared.foundIn: Crossref search « Not learning from failure the greatest failure of all » (2026-11-23); line of research named in the idea scout's notes

population: adults in 5 experiments (total N = 1,674), binary-choice questions; online samples (MTurk according to Gok & Fyfe 2024); countries not given in the abstract

findings.text: People told they had answered wrong learned less, on a follow-up test, than people told they had answered right, although both kinds of feedback gave away the correct answer

support.sentence: However, on a follow-up test, participants learned less from failure feedback than from success feedback.

findings.text: The authors explain the gap by ego threat: a personal failure makes people tune out (their interpretation; Gok & Fyfe 2024 did not find the ego-threat difference)

support.sentence: Failure is ego threatening, which causes people to tune out.

findings.text: People learned less from their own failure than from their own success, but showed no reliable difference between learning from others' failures and from others' successes (a non-significant difference, not an equivalence test)

support.sentence: Participants learned less from personal failure than from personal success, yet they learned just as much from other people's failure as from others' success.

limits: laboratory: binary-choice questions about an unknown script, learning tested minutes later; not failures in life
Spiller 2025 (Psychological Science): the task's scoring marks consistent answers right after success, wrong after failure; a preregistered study without feedback reproduced the gap
the authors replied in 2025 (Psychological Science) that consistency does not explain their original paradigm, without new data in the abstract: the debate is open
the ego-threat explanation was not found by Gok & Fyfe 2024 (no ego-threat difference; task-focused feedback did not shrink the gap)
« just as much » (others' failures) is a non-significant difference, not an equivalence test; Spiller also explains it by the absence of the consistency bias
full text not read; the replications (Keith 2022, Gok 2024) use the same task, so they do not escape its scoring problem
